Each link below was checked this session and loads.

- **[21 CFR 606.171 — Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/606.171)**
  — the reportability test this module's packet applies (and fails to show its reasoning on):
  the two-prong test in paragraph (b), and the 45-day reporting clock in paragraph (c). Local
  verbatim copy: `sources/cfr/606.171.md`.

- **[21 CFR 606.100 — Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/606.100)**
  — paragraph (b)(16)'s labeling-safeguards requirement (new to this course) and paragraph (c)'s
  "conclusions and followup" investigation standard, both central to this module's reveal. Local
  verbatim copy: `sources/cfr/606.100.md`.

- **[21 CFR 606.160 — Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/606.160)**
  — paragraph (b)(7)(iii), the general-records requirement behind the deviation record itself.
  Local verbatim copy: `sources/cfr/606.160.md`.

- **[Pushing Beyond Human Error in Root Cause Analysis](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=D8u5PwuHkUI)**
  (PathWise, from oEmbed `author_name`) — the video embedded in this lesson. A root-cause-analysis
  training firm on why "human error" is where an investigation should start asking questions, not
  where it should stop — the same test this lesson applies to a QA's draft. Commercial training
  content, not a regulator or standards body, and not blood-specific. Verified embeddable via
  YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[ECA Academy: Root Cause Analysis and CAPA — Why FDA Keeps Calling Them Out](https://www.gmp-compliance.org/gmp-news/root-cause-analysis-and-capa-why-fda-keeps-calling-them-out)**
  — an article from the ECA Foundation's GMP news service reviewing recent FDA Warning Letters
  where shallow investigations and corrective actions that missed systemic causes were cited.
  Read it to see, in real citations, the "stopped at the first plausible cause" pattern this
  module's root-cause finding is built on. Drug and device examples, not blood-specific. Verified
  loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[ECA Academy: When "Undetermined" is not an Answer — what two FDA Warning Letters show about root cause analysis and CAPA](https://www.gmp-compliance.org/gmp-news/when-undetermined-is-not-an-answer-what-two-fda-warning-letters-show-about-root-cause-analysis-and-capa)**
  — two Warning Letters in which investigations were closed before the true cause was found or the
  full product risk assessed, and FDA's conclusion that investigation quality determines CAPA
  quality. A good companion to this module's evidence-and-extent question. Verified loading via
  `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[Hogan Lovells: Closing the CAPA is not closing the loop](https://hlc.com/en/publications/closing-the-capa-is-not-closing-the-loop)**
  — a law-firm article arguing that completing a CAPA's actions shows only implementation, and that
  effectiveness needs predefined, objective criteria tied to the root cause. This is the written
  version of this module's "could this check fail?" test. Device-focused. Verified loading via
  `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[Cureus (via PubMed Central): Enhancing Pharmaceutical Product Quality With a Comprehensive CAPA Framework: From Reactive to Proactive](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11490658/)**
  — a 2024 peer-reviewed review walking through the stages of a CAPA process, from risk assessment
  and root cause analysis through effectiveness review, and the regulatory expectations behind
  them. Read it for a vocabulary and structure check on the whole CAPA lifecycle. Verified loading
  via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[FDA: Biological Product Deviations](https://www.fda.gov/vaccines-blood-biologics/report-problem-center-biologics-evaluation-research/biological-product-deviations)**
  — FDA's CBER page on reporting biological product deviations, the regulator's own entry point
  for the 606.171 reportability decision this module's packet states without reasoning. Read it
  alongside 606.171 when deciding what a defensible reportability write-up has to show. Verified
  loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[FDA: Warning Letters](https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/compliance-actions-and-activities/warning-letters)**
  — FDA's searchable database of published Warning Letters. Search it by "investigation" or
  "root cause" to read, in the regulator's own words, how weak investigations and unverified CAPAs
  are actually cited. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

## Keep learning

Not official sources — good places to learn more about reviewing investigations, root cause and CAPA.

- **[Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA): The Definitive Guide](https://thefdagroup.com/blog/definitive-guide-to-capa)** (The FDA Group, consultancy) — A step-by-step walk through the CAPA lifecycle, ending in effectiveness verification. Consultancy marketing content, but a clear checklist for what a complete write-up contains. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[Two Audit Case Studies Reveal the Cost of Incomplete Corrective Actions](https://www.pharmtech.com/view/two-audit-case-studies-reveal-the-cost-of-incomplete-corrective-actions)** (Pharmaceutical Technology) — Trade-press case studies of corrective actions that were closed but not completed. Good concrete examples for reviewing the "did it actually work" part of a CAPA. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[Five whys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Five_whys)** (Wikipedia) — A quick overview of the technique, including its limitations, so you can judge whether an analyst's "why chain" is genuinely causal. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
